The first three months of the year are January, February, and March.

The theory of relativity, developed by Albert Einstein, fundamentally changed how we understand the universe by linking space, time, and gravity. It consists of two main parts: special relativity, which is used in particle physics and cosmology, and general relativity, which explains how gravity works. According to this theory, massive objects like stars and planets warp the fabric of space and time around them. This warping is what we experience as gravity, effectively describing how matter and energy influence the structure of the universe.
